- If sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- If sentiment is strongly bearish (≤ -0.50), model often underestimates downside; add buffer or adjust downward bias.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior day), model frequently overshoots; apply decay or smoothing to subsequent forecasts.
- When sentiment shifts abruptly (e.g., from bullish to bearish), model lags in adjusting; prioritize early correction in forecast horizon.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., after 70+ peak, price drops sharply), model often fails to anticipate; add momentum decay factor.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to overfit recent trends; reduce weight on recent history if sentiment is volatile or mixed.
- If sentiment history shows high volatility (alternating +/– 0.5+), model should be more conservative; avoid steep upward/downward trends.
- When true outcome deviates >5% from 14-day moving average, model often misjudges trend; use moving average as anchor for correction.
